summary: Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a Tibetologist. He studied under George de Roerich and under traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.
Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1937–1942) and later served as a professor there (~1950–1987).

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Chizan Senmon Gakko, under Shoko Watanabe, and at Tohoku University. His career included professorships at Koyasan University and Nagoya University, as well as roles at Chisan Denpōin and Shuchiin University.

Yusho Wakahara (b. 1952) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami. He lectured at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and served as assistant professor (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013) at Ryukoku University.
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he served as emeritus professor (~1970–2005).

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who earned a doctorate from Kyushu University. He worked at the Nara National Cultural Properties Research Institute (~1956–1973), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2004).

Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Toru Haneda, Hidenaka Tanaka, Gyoyu Tokiwai, and Naoshiro Tsuji, he held professorships at Tokyo University of Science, Tokai University, Kyoto Tachibana University, and Soka University.

Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda. He has held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania, under scholars including Ashikaga, Renou, Brown, and Minard. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986) and held a post at Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi (b. 1928) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and was a professor at Rissho University (~1973–1999).

Yutaka Yoshida (b. 1954) specializes in history, Japanology, and linguistics. Educated at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo, he taught at Hitotsubashi University (1983–2018; emeritus 2018) and held posts at Kyoto University and other research centers.

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hajime Nakamura and earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as assistant professor at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Yutang Lin (1895–1976) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and Leipzig University under August Conrady, and held a post at Peking University (~1916–1926).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) was a Sinologist and philosopher educated at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University (1978), the University of Tokyo (1981–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2003).

Yönten Gyatso (1932–2002) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He obtained a Geshé degree from Drepung Gomang Dratsang, earned a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and served as a research advisor there (~1981–1997).
Yōhei Kawashiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2011).
Yūki Takamu specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Takamu pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yūto Kawamura is an Indologist who completed a postdoc at Kyoto University (2015–2018). Kawamura held positions at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).
Zack Beer is a student in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Zaifu Liu (1941–2026) studied at Xiamen University and worked in Sinology. He directed the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (1985–1989) and lectured at the University of Chicago, Stockholm University, and the University of Colorado Boulder.
